annotation.title_clean: Smart Robots and Civil Liability in Jordan: A Quest for Legal Synthesis in the Age of Automation
annotation.title_en: Smart Robots and Civil Liability in Jordan: A Quest for Legal Synthesis in the Age of Automation
annotation.venue: Jordanian Journal of Law and Political Science
named_instruments_referenced: EU Civil Law Rules on Robotics 2017
annotation.summary_en: Doctrinal legal article analysing whether Jordanian civil liability rules (contractual, tortious, custodian liability) can address harm caused by AI-powered smart robots, comparing with EU developments. It finds major gaps and proposes legislative intervention, AI legal personality, global accountability standards and international cooperation.
key_provisions_or_claims: Jordan's civil law has a vacuum on AI-induced liability, with no judicial precedents.
Traditional objective and personal liability theories apply poorly to unpredictable autonomous AI.
Proposes granting AI a legal personality.
Calls for legislative intervention and global accountability standards.
Recommends international cooperation and ethical programming of technological limits.
